t:
The amount of the reduction in the appropriation “Repair Facilities, Navy”, provided for in title VII of the National Military Establishment Appropriation Act, 1950, is hereby changed to $18,448,439.

Appropriations under the head “Repair Facilities, Navy”, shall not be available for expenditure after June 30, 1950, except for payment of claims certified under the Surplus Fund—Certified Claims Act of 1949. Any unexpended balances remaining on said date shall revert to the Treasury in the manner provided by said Act for lapsed appropriations and the account shall be abolished.

fable.w: This section only adjusts an appropriation reduction and sets the lapse and reversion of funds to the Treasury. The tempting reading is that the reference to "claims certified" involves outside parties, but paying certified claims is a payment mechanism, not consultation with or a right to challenge a federal decision by anyone outside the government. No comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue is involved.
fable.s: Appropriations under the head “Repair Facilities, Navy”, shall not be available for expenditure after June 30, 1950, except for payment of claims certified under the Surplus Fund—Certified Claims Act of 1949.

qwen_block.w: This section is a purely fiscal provision that adjusts the amount of a specific appropriation and sets expiration dates for its use. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public hearings, or requirements for input from states, tribes, or the public.
qwen_block.s: The amount of the reduction in the appropriation “Repair Facilities, Navy”, provided for in title VII of the National Military Establishment Appropriation Act, 1950, is hereby changed to $18,448,439.

opus.w: This section only changes the amount an appropriation is reduced by, sets the date after which the money can no longer be spent, and sends unspent balances back to the Treasury. The reference to certified claims is an exception to the spending deadline. It does not give any outside party a way to take part in, or challenge, a federal decision. No one outside the federal government is consulted or involved.
opus.s: Appropriations under the head “Repair Facilities, Navy”, shall not be available for expenditure after June 30, 1950, except for payment of claims certified under the Surplus Fund—Certified Claims Act of 1949.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The phrase "payment of claims certified under the Surplus Fund—Certified Claims Act of 1949" could look like outside parties pressing claims against the government. It fails because it only says what the leftover money can still be spent on. It sets up no consultation, hearing, advisory body or right to sue. Paying a certified claim is a matter of handling money, not outside involvement in a decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section deals exclusively with the adjustment of appropriation amounts and the expiration of funds for a specific Navy account. It does not establish any process for consulting with, coordinating with, or receiving input from parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private entities) before making a decision. The reference to certified claims is a procedural detail regarding existing legal mechanisms, not a new participation requirement defined in this text.
qwen_chat.s: The amount of the reduction in the appropriation “Repair Facilities, Navy”, provided for in title VII of the National Military Establishment Appropriation Act, 1950, is hereby changed to $18,448,439.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the mention of "claims certified under the Surplus Fund—Certified Claims Act of 1949" implies a process where outside parties (claimants) participate. However, the section itself does not describe the participation process; it merely sets a deadline for expenditures and references an existing act for claim certification. The core of the section is about budgetary limits and account abolition, not about establishing a new mechanism for public or external participation in a federal decision. The definition requires the section itself to involve consultation, coordination, or decision-making with outsiders. This section is purely administrative and financial.
